problem: Prove a lower bound on the variance-scaled Turán deficit Vδ_D at the first descent of Poisson-binomial mass functions, establishing that Vδ_D ≥ 1/4.
gap: Existing bounds on δ_k depend on the number of summands n or individual success probabilities and degenerate when many summands have p_i near 0 or 1 at fixed variance, whereas a variance-alone bound is absent.
contribution: We prove Vδ_D ≥ 1/4, show this is tight up to a constant (1/3 is optimal), derive δ_k bounds at every support index, and establish applications to eigenvalue counts in random unitary matrices, via exact-arithmetic Bernstein expansions.
note: Technically sound and on-topic for ECP, but the opening does not name the debate this enters or establish why this variance-scaled bound matters for the field.
